The next hearing on November 17. Jocelyn Fernandes Updated 4 Nov 2026, 07:47 AM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Key demands from Punjab state government employees include — payment of pending 18% DA, implementation of Old Pension Scheme (OPS), regularisation of contractual employees, implementation of minimum wages for workers. ( AI generated image ) AI Quick Read DA arrears case: The Punjab and Haryana High Court held a hearing in the state'state's pending dearness allowance case on Tuesday, 3 November, PTI reported. And in its order has issued a contempt notice to the Chief Secretary of Punjab, besides ordering the authority to file a reply via a compliance affidavit within 10 days. The affidavit will be on the state's previous non-compliance of the HC's order dated 3 August, it said. The next hearing is scheduled on 17 November, it added. Also Read | DA hike: Tamil Nadu, MP, Rajasthan—States with Diwali dearness allowance hikes Punjab DA arrears case: Latest updates The bench heard both sides and issued a contempt notice to the Chief Secretary of Punjab, who was present in the courtroom. I t also imposed a fine of ₹ 1 lakh on the Punjab Chief Secretary for non-compliance with its orders. It directed the Chief Secretary to file a reply via a compliance affidavit within 10 days explaining non-compliance with the High Court's earlier order dated August 3. The state government on its part told the court that its Special Leave Petition (SLP) is ready for filing after curing all procedural defects. The state added that the matter is likely to be listed before the Supreme Court immediately after Diwali. Also Read | 8th Pay Commission: How arrears will be paid after recommendations, explained Meanwhile, counsel representing the petitioners argued that the state is facing a financial emergency and urged the Court to restrain the government from spending public funds on freebies. Highlighting the court's strict stance against the administrative delay, Senior Advocate Sunny Singla stated, “The issue reached the High Court again after employees sought action against state officials for failing to implement the August 3 order. The petitioners' counsel submitted that the state government neither disbursed the DA arrears within the stipulated timeframe nor filed the mandatory compliance report sought by the Court.” What happened? The case so far… Earlier in October, the court heard a case concerning pending DA arrears of Punjab government employees and pensioners and took a stern view of the state’s failure to comply with its orders. Also Read | NPS rules changed: PFRDA revises these scheme names, clarifies PoP display norms The hearing was held on a contempt petition filed by Nirmal Singh Dhillon, a retired Chief Engineer of Punjab State Power Corporation Limited (PSPCL), over the alleged non-compliance with court directions regarding DA)and Dearness Relief (DR). During the hearing before the bench of Justice Harsh Bunger, the counsel representing the employees submitted that the Punjab government was adopting delaying tactics to avoid implementing the HC's orders. The counsel also pointed out that the SLP filed by the state before the SC remained on the defect list for more than two months. During the proceedings, the court made strong observations and questioned why the government had withheld DA/DR benefits from employees but had not similarly withheld the benefits of its senior officials.
